boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.37.36, “Then Yahweh’s angel went out and struck one hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. boundary_rationale: This unit opens at web:Isa.40.1, “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God., pointed נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ עַמִּ֑י יֹאמַ֖ר אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1, tier: byte), a doubled imperative command to comfort, closed by a postpositive inquit that names God by the ordinary divine-title word. That inquit, אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם, is the Elohim variant and stands outside the 52-verse amar-plus-tetragrammaton adjacency census; it is also distinct from the 23-verse postpositive divine-signature census whose own narrative-zone site is נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.37.34, tier: byte). The command is filled out at web:Isa.40.2, “Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”, pointed דַּבְּר֞וּ עַל לֵ֤ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וְקִרְא֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֤י מָֽלְאָה֙ צְבָאָ֔הּ כִּ֥י נִרְצָ֖ה עֲוֺנָ֑הּ כִּ֤י לָקְחָה֙ מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה כִּפְלַ֖יִם בְּכָל חַטֹּאתֶֽיהָ (oshb:Isa.40.2, tier: byte), addressed to unnamed comforters instructed to speak to Jerusalem's heart. The verse directly ahead of this unit's own opening material, oshb:Isa.39.8, carries a PE parashah mark, attested in a single witness, at its own close. This unit's own closing verse, oshb:Isa.40.2, ends under a parashah SAMEKH mark (single-witness), which backs the coming division right before the next voice-onset at oshb:Isa.40.3.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through web:Isa.40.3-Isa.40.5 was weighed and declined, since a fresh voice-onset opens with ק֣וֹל קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3, tier: byte), the sole verse-initial site of that calling-voice onset in the book (sweep: 1 verse), distinct from the comforters addressed in web:Isa.40.1-Isa.40.2.
literature_type_guess: opening comfort command with a divine-title inquit variant

device_notes: The imperatives carrying this command are plural in form — נַחֲמ֥וּ נַחֲמ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.40.1, tier: byte) and דַּבְּר֞וּ … וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2, tier: byte) — a byte-checkable feature of the letters themselves rather than a claim resting on the unstaged morphology layer; the plural is what leaves the addressee open to more than one comforter. The attribution of those plural comforters is not named in the bytes; this row holds that question open rather than assigning a speaker. The postpositive inquit at web:Isa.40.1 is registered as a divine-speech-frame variant because its own closing word, אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1, tier: byte), spells the ordinary divine-title form; that is the ground for the variant tag, argued from the onset's own bytes rather than from any vocabulary allowance.
